key_gap: On a fully specified power-law portfolio problem both reached the identical decision (Strategy B, EV $215M vs $185M, +$30M) with the same full sensitivity set: follow-on effectiveness breakeven f* = 0.625, tail hit rate required for the 3x target p* = 2.7%, tail dominance 27%/29%, and the counterfactual that 25 checks of $4M (undifferentiated) equal Strategy A. The AI's gap is efficiency: it spent extra passes (stage narration, premortem, decision packet) on arithmetic that was checkable from the given inputs, while the pure-style baseline delivered the same result, breakevens, and counterfactual in a single linear pass.
learning_signal: On fully specified power-law portfolio math, the load-bearing moves are exactly: per-check EV from the power-law distribution (weighted by hit rates), linearity to portfolio EV, follow-on uplift with idle-capital accounting, tail-share quantification, breakevens on the free parameters (follow-on effectiveness, tail rate), and the undifferentiated-check counterfactual. Extended narrative and packet structure add no decision value on these problems and cost tokens; the benchmark to close is the pure style's one-pass exactness.
suggested_improvement: In HOW, add a route rule for fully-specified portfolio-arithmetic problems: compress to 'per-check EV -> scale by linearity -> add follow-on uplift and idle-capital return -> select max -> breakeven sensitivity on free parameters -> one counterfactual check'; keep verification as inline arithmetic (e.g., EV(B) = base + uplift, and expected follow-on count x check size + idle at par), and skip extended meta-narrative; reserve the full stage structure and packet for problems with uncertain or incomplete inputs.

key_gap: Pure portfolio-EV recommended investing $10M (claimed EV $12.75M > $10M, '27.5% margin'), treating the asserted 2% $2B-exit probability as a measurement: 78.4% of the EV sits in that bucket, which has no measurement channel (zero exits in category, empty reference class); breakeven tail p* = 1.45% exceeds every plausible base-rate estimate (0.2-0.8%, EV $3.75M-$6.75M = a loss) and breakeven ownership s* = 78.4% is impossible at $40M post. The AI declined: it rejected the EV as notional, quantified tail dominance, computed the decision-flip breakevens, compared the 27.5% claimed margin against the ±4x estimation error, and capped exposure at a token.
learning_signal: Portfolio EV is necessary but not sufficient when the distribution is power-law: before selecting on EV, the agent must (a) compute tail dominance (share of EV in the top bucket) — if one low-probability bucket carries most of the EV, the decision is a tail bet; (b) check the measurement validity of that probability: does a reference class or base rate exist? Asserted-without-channel probabilities must be labeled notional; (c) compute decision-flip breakevens (breakeven tail probability, breakeven ownership/price) and compare the claimed margin against the plausible estimation error — if error exceeds margin, the EV comparison is noise; (d) when the tail is unmeasurable, size the decision so the error cannot hurt (decline or token), and demand reference-class evidence before repricing.
suggested_improvement: Add a mandatory measurement-validity gate in HOW before selection on any EV table whose value is dominated by a single low-probability bucket: (1) compute top-bucket EV share; if > ~50%, flag 'tail-dominated EV'; (2) require a reference class for the tail probability — if none exists, mark the input NOTIONAL and exclude it from selection; (3) compute breakevens (tail probability and ownership) and the pessimistic re-estimate at the plausible base-rate range; (4) demote any action whose margin is smaller than the tail-parameter error, label the packet status APPROXIMATED with the EV bound, and default to decline or token-sized exposure; record the evidence requirement in the decision packet.
